subject: NAs not allowed when no NAs present

messages.author: 3425858b9b48ea14
messages.subject: NAs not allowed when no NAs present
parts:
Hey All,

When I run the following code I get an error message saying that NAs are not allowed, however I do not have NAs in my data. If I do not use a regression between B and C but a covariance, the error message does not show up.

Can anyone help me out?

femalecov <- matrix(c(1.00, .86, -.8, .29,
                      .86, 1.00, -.79, .3,
                      -.80, -.79, 1.00, -.33,
                      .29, .30, -.33, 1.00),4,4)
rownames(femalecov) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")
colnames(femalecov) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")

modFemales <- '
A ~~ D
B ~ C
A ~~ B
A ~~ C
'
fitFemales <- sem(modFemales, sample.cov=femalecov, sample.nobs=246)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: NAs not allowed when no NAs present
parts:
Are you running the latest version of lavaan?  I get an error, but I don't get the same error as you, even when I specify (as it seems you should) the option sem(..., fixed.x = FALSE)

> fitFemales <- sem(modFemales, sample.cov=femalecov, sample.nobs=246, fixed.x = FALSE)
Error in lav_model(lavpartable = lavpartable, representation = lavoptions$representation,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: parameter is not defined: A ~~ D


I'm not sure whether the error message has anything to do with an identification problem, but I don't think your model is identified.  You are positing that C affects B, and that A is related to both C and the residuals of B.  I think this is what is called a non-recursive model.  Typically in path analysis, you allow all exogenous variables to freely covary (in your model, A, C, and D), and exogenous variables effect endogenous variables (B) but remain uncorrelated with their disturbance/error terms.  Not to say that this is your hypothesized model, but this, for instance, works fine:

> modFemales <- 'B ~ C + A + D'
> fitFemales <- sem(modFemales, sample.cov=femalecov, sample.nobs=246, fixed.x = FALSE)
> summary(fitFemales)
